clue.text: Action to be taken about the French gun handed over

indicators.note: the action word is to wrap itself around the following pieces, so it is the container

parts.note: a deed is an action
le is French for the
gat is old slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Someone describes a weapon passed across while some action is planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Duties handed over to a deputy have been passed on to them in this sense.

clue.text: Specialist making small change in exercise

indicators.note: the coin goes inside the exercise word

parts.note: to exert is to exercise, as in exerting influence
p is a penny, small change

explanation.surface: A specialist makes a minor tweak to a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert is an authority, a specialist in a field.

clue.text: With monstrous head and sickening cry and ears like wings" Chesterton (The Donkey)

definitions.text: With monstrous head and sickening cry and ears like wings" Chesterton (The Donkey)

parts.words: With monstrous head and sickening cry and ears like wings" Chesterton (The Donkey)
parts.note: a quotation from Chesterton's poem with one word missing before wings, to be supplied from memory

explanation.surface: A line of verse describing a donkey's ugly head and loud bray.
explanation.definitionFit: In the poem the donkey's ears are likened to wandering wings, astray and roving.

clue.text: Song setting a conservationist body on edge

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, which looks after historic British places
a hem is the edge of cloth

explanation.surface: A tune puts an environmental group on its toes.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a solemn song, such as a national hymn.

clue.text: Getting in range possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may form something other than written

explanation.surface: Someone is coming into range, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Earning is gaining money, so getting in the sense of acquiring.

clue.text: Keen for action?

parts.note: keen is read as a wail or shout rather than eager, so this is a shout raised for combat

explanation.surface: Someone eager to get going.
explanation.definitionFit: A rallying shout before combat is a wail or cry made for fighting.

clue.text: The underworld, being on the level, scoffed-so incongruous

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and its name
par means equal, on a level
scoffed means ate greedily

explanation.surface: Hell, being honest, mocked the oddity of it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffed' reads as jeered but means wolfed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Disparate things are unlike each other, so they do not fit together.

clue.text: A reckless guy's road speed varied greatly

indicators.note: the letters are changed greatly, which signals that they are shuffled

explanation.surface: A tearaway's speed on the road went up and down wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a bold outlaw willing to take any risk.

clue.text: Bringing a hundred into line is quite easy

indicators.note: the article and the hundred are brought inside the line, so this word marks the insertion

parts.note: a file is a line of people one behind another
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Straightening a hundred things into a row turns out to be simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Something facile is achieved with little effort, a synonym of simple.

clue.text: Musical high-spots for the workers

parts.note: an opera is a musical stage work
tors are rocky hilltops, high spots on moorland

explanation.surface: The best moments of a show are laid on to please the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Operators are people who run machines, a general term for workers.

clue.text: Close or street with not a single dog

parts.note: not a single one is nought, the round letter O
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: A cul-de-sac or road where no dogs at all are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a noun for a quiet road beside 'street', but it is the verb to shut.
explanation.definitionFit: To block a hole or a pipe is to seal it off, a verb meaning shut.

clue.text: Translation of "The Butterfly" making a poet grin

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are worked into something new, which signals a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A poet smiles at a translated title about a butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translation of' sits as a link: rearranging the butterfly's name makes A POET GRIN, as the clue playfully claims.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a British butterfly whose males have orange wingtips.

clue.text: Blunder by trusted leader causing great consternation

indicators.note: the first letter stands beside the mistake, placed before it
the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: an error is a blunder

explanation.surface: A trusted chief makes a mistake and alarm spreads.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror is overwhelming fear, which great consternation describes.

clue.text: Compass acknowledgments of debt, and that's enterprising

parts.note: ambit is scope or compass
IOUs are notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: A range of credit notes suggests a go-getting businessman.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambitious person is eager to get on, full of drive.

clue.text: Mostly in deep water

definitions.meaning: out on the open sea, the main being the ocean

explanation.surface: Someone is largely in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means generally, and literally out on the ocean, which poets call the main.

clue.text: Moving after professional encouragement

indicators.note: the movement word comes after the professional

parts.note: pro is short for professional
motion is movement, moving

explanation.surface: A coach's urging gets a player moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion is furtherance, active support that helps something advance.

clue.text: An article for example backing seniority

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: backing means the abbreviation is read from its end to its start

explanation.surface: Someone backs a piece of writing to illustrate who ranks highest.
explanation.definitionFit: Seniority is a matter of being older, of greater years.

clue.text: A record height

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A new record altitude is reached.
explanation.definitionFit: An alp is a high mountain, a lofty elevation.

clue.text: Some rather feeble weak-willed sheepish creature

indicators.note: some of the letters of the words that follow are taken, a run spanning them

explanation.surface: A rather timid and spineless person who acts like a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe is a female sheep, so literally a sheepish animal.

clue.text: The collier needs a pound to get adrink

definitions.note: the page runs together the words a drink

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner
L stands for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A coal miner needs money for a pint after his shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Mineral water, or a fizzy soft drink called a mineral, is a kind of beverage.

clue.text: Crushed to produce fine stuff

definitions.meaning: a smooth woollen cloth made from long combed fibres

explanation.surface: Something is pressed down to make fine material.
explanation.definitionFit: Being outdone is to be beaten; the same spelling names a smooth woollen yarn and fabric.

clue.text: Food-mixed type

definitions.meaning: a printer's term for a jumble of spilled type, also spelt pi

explanation.surface: Food comes out as a jumble of kinds.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry dish is a common meal; printers called scrambled type by the same name.

clue.text: Not punctilious in previous work

parts.note: ex means former or previous
an act is a work or deed

explanation.surface: Someone was careless in an earlier job.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inexact means lacking precision, the opposite of scrupulous care.

clue.text: Fashionable buzz as last of wine is being put down

parts.note: in means fashionable
a hum is a buzz

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A trendy party buzzes as the last of the wine is drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhume is to bury, putting a body down into the ground.

clue.text: A carrier of young

definitions.meaning: a stretcher or couch on poles for bearing people

explanation.surface: Someone carrying offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a stretcher for bearing people and a brood of baby animals.

clue.text: Taking one in sordid surroundings is excusable

indicators.note: the corrupt word takes in the numeral, holding it inside

parts.note: venal means corrupt, sordidly mercenary
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Accepting someone into a seedy setting can be forgiven.
explanation.definitionFit: A venial sin is a pardonable one, minor enough to be forgiven.

clue.text: Border revolutionary arming

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests overturning the order of the letters

explanation.surface: Rebels take up weapons on the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is an edge or boundary of something.

clue.text: A male vied for representation in years gone by

indicators.note: a new representation of the letters means they are set out in another order

explanation.surface: A man competes to be depicted in an old-fashioned portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediaeval refers to the Middle Ages, a period long past.

clue.text: Anyone living in a house requires a certain amount of curtain material

definitions.text: Anyone living in a house requires

indicators.note: a certain amount of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Every household needs some fabric for its curtains.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate originally meant any occupant of a dwelling, one who lives in it.

clue.text: Some crest! Some bird!

parts.note: part means some of something
a ridge is the crest of a hill

explanation.surface: An exclamation of admiration at a bird's plumed head.
explanation.definitionFit: A partridge is a game bird, one particular species.

clue.text: Concert's acceptable-no bad thing, looking back

definitions.note: the possessive stands for concert is

parts.note: U is upper-class, hence acceptable

indicators.note: looking back means the words are read backwards

parts.note: a sin is a bad thing

explanation.surface: A reviewer finds a concert fine, nothing wrong when thinking back.
explanation.definitionFit: In concert means acting together, in agreement or harmony.

clue.text: Setting out about fifty would be most surprising

indicators.note: the departure word goes around the numeral, marking a container

parts.note: starting means setting out
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Departing with around fifty in tow would cause amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling means alarming or astonishing, a synonym of surprising.
